title: Global Markets Under Pressure: AI Spending Concerns Trigger Tech Selloff as Oil Surges and Bitcoin Slides
intro: Global financial markets closed a turbulent session in deeply mixed territory, as mounting concerns over the sustainability of artificial intelligence capital expenditure triggered a significant rotation out of technology shares. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.4%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average each shed 0.3%. Against this backdrop, the Russell 2000 outperformed with a 1.0% gain, reflecting a decisive rotation toward small-cap equities and defensive sectors. Compounding market unease, stronger-than-expected US GDP growth and persistently elevated inflation introduced fresh uncertainty into the Federal Reserve's policy trajectory, while geopolitical tensions in the Middle East propelled crude oil to six-week highs. Bitcoin retreated sharply toward $76,000 and Gold slipped below $4,000, underscoring the broad-based volatility now permeating global asset classes.

sections.heading: Technology Stocks Lead Wall Street Lower as AI Spending Concerns Intensify
sections.content: The technology sector bore the brunt of the session's selling pressure, as institutional investors moved to reassess whether the scale of AI-related capital deployment can generate commensurate returns. Alphabet plunged 12.6% following weaker-than-expected revenue figures, softening search growth trends and a materially higher AI spending profile. ServiceNow dropped 27% and Fortinet lost 20% after both companies delivered disappointing earnings and forward guidance. Caterpillar declined 9% amid concerns over the durability of AI-driven data-center investment cycles. After the close, Amazon fell approximately 7% while Intel plunged around 23% following a deteriorating outlook. Not all names moved lower, however. Crocs surged 25.5%, Gen Digital gained 15.8%, Carvana advanced 16%, and ADT jumped 33% following the announcement of its $15.3 billion acquisition agreement with Thrive Holdings. On a sector basis, Healthcare gained 2.6% and Real Estate rose 2.3%, with eight of the eleven S&P 500 sectors ultimately closing in positive territory — a dynamic that underscores the rotation underway rather than broad-based market deterioration.

sections.heading: US Macro Data Remains Resilient, but Inflation Complicates the Fed's Path
sections.content: On the macroeconomic front, the US economy demonstrated continued resilience. GDP expanded at an annualized rate of 3.4% in Q3, exceeding consensus expectations of 3.2%, underpinned by robust consumer spending and sustained AI-related investment activity. However, inflationary pressures remain a key complicating factor for monetary policy. September's PCE price index rose 0.5% month over month, bringing the annual rate to 3.6%, while Core PCE inflation held at 3.1% — both readings that maintain meaningful distance from the Federal Reserve's 2% target. The Fed opted to hold interest rates unchanged at its most recent meeting, yet the combination of above-trend growth and sticky inflation has materially reinforced market expectations for a potential December rate hike. The interplay between economic strength and persistent price pressures continues to represent the central policy dilemma facing the FOMC heading into year-end.

sections.heading: Commodities and Crypto: Oil Climbs, Gold Slips, Bitcoin Under Pressure
sections.content: Crude oil emerged as one of the session's clearest outperformers. WTI climbed above $103 per barrel, reaching six-week highs, as renewed US-Iran tensions escalated concerns over potential military conflict and supply disruption risk. Uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz and regional shipping corridors continues to provide structural support to energy prices, notwithstanding reports that crude exports have broadly recovered toward pre-conflict levels. Oil has now gained more than 10% in October, with geopolitical developments functioning as the primary price driver. Gold extended its decline below $4,000 per ounce, pressured by rising expectations for a more restrictive monetary policy stance. The precious metal is tracking toward an almost 4% monthly loss, potentially recording its second consecutive monthly decline — raising the fundamental question of whether this constitutes a sustained trend reversal or a technical correction following the prior rally. Bitcoin fell to $76,000, its lowest level since mid-September, as security concerns surrounding Binance intensified selling pressure. The incident reportedly involved an estimated $6.3 billion in affected assets, with approximately $3 billion frozen through blockchain partners. Around $1.3 billion in bullish crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours ahead of an $11 billion options expiry on Deribit. Despite the weakness, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $423.7 million in net inflows between Monday and Wednesday, signaling that institutional conviction in the asset class has not materially deteriorated. Rounding out the cross-asset picture, the US Dollar Index slipped toward 101.5, extending losses for a third consecutive session, while the 10-year Treasury yield declined toward 4.9% — a seven-week low — as investors rotated into government bonds amid concerns over technology valuations and elevated AI spending risk.

quote: Eight of eleven S&P 500 sectors closed higher even as the Nasdaq fell 1.4% — a structural rotation signal that institutional investors should not underestimate heading into year-end.
conclusion: Global markets are increasingly navigating a complex intersection of resilient macroeconomic fundamentals and mounting risks across corporate valuations, inflation dynamics, and geopolitical flashpoints. The rotation from technology into defensive and small-cap equities may deepen if AI spending concerns persist through the upcoming earnings cycle, while Federal Reserve policy expectations will remain acutely sensitive to incoming PCE and CPI data. In commodities, crude oil's trajectory will be disproportionately influenced by developments in the Middle East, particularly any escalation involving the Strait of Hormuz. For risk assets broadly, the balance between economic resilience and rising uncertainty will likely serve as the decisive variable determining the next significant directional move. Volatility, by all indications, remains structurally elevated.
excerpt: Tech selloff, AI spending fears, oil above $103, Bitcoin at $76,000 and mixed macro data define a volatile global market session.
